topic: Thread State Management: Conditions for Non-Joinability
explanation: A `std::thread` object is considered safe for destruction only when it is non-joinable. A thread transitions to a non-joinable state under three specific conditions: 1) It has been successfully `join()`ed (the underlying execution has completed and resources cleaned up). 2) It has been successfully `detach()`ed (the object has severed its connection to the underlying execution, which continues independently). 3) It has been moved *from* (the thread handle ownership has been transferred to another `std::thread` object). Checking `t.joinable()` is essential before calling `join()` or allowing destruction.
practical_example: When implementing a thread-owning RAII wrapper, the wrapper's destructor must check `if (t.joinable())` before deciding whether to call `join()` or `detach()` to ensure the thread is handled and the program avoids termination.
chapter: Item 37: Make std::thread s unjoinable on all paths.
